newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Sen. Roth says $143 bln net tax cuts minimum.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Sen. Roth says $143 bln net tax cuts minimum.

text.p: Senate Finance Committee Chairman William Roth wrote Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott that $143 billion in net tax cuts over five years were a "bare minimum," according to a letter obtained Friday.
"In order to provide both family tax relief and promote long term economic growth, the net tax cut must be significant and larger than the press reports of $80 billion," Roth wrote.
"My view is that roughly $143 billion in net tax cuts over five years is really the bare minimum..." the Delaware Republican said.
Roth said net savings of $115 billion to $120 billion in Medicare would be "much more realistic" than the reported $130 billion in net savings under discussion.
For Medicaid, net savings of $20 billion to $25 billion "are appropriate and attainable" within the committee, he said.
"Clearly any policy decisions to reach these targets should be left to our committee and I would ask that this be kept in mind as you proceed this week," Roth said in the letter dated April 23.

Roth urged that if there was a move to adjust the consumer price index that it be a full adjustment of 1.1 percentage points. An advisory commission last December said the CPI overstated cost-of-living by 1.1 percentage points.
Congressional and White House budget negotiators have been trying to reach agreement on budget issues.
